from zelda.emulator import LOGS_DIR
CKPT = LOGS_DIR / "checkpoints"

def timeline(name: str) -> list[tuple[int, int, str]]:
    """(start_frame, end_frame, segment) for the real run, in order.

    The checkpoint directory still holds files from abandoned route branches (l4_stairs,
    whirl_back1, x8_2e ...). Globbing it drops those names into the middle of Level 1, so
    trust only the segment list recorded inside the newest checkpoint.
    """
    metas = {}
    for p in CKPT.glob(f"{name}_*.json"):
        d = json.loads(p.read_text())
        if d.get("segments"):
            metas[d["segments"][-1]] = d
    if not metas:
        return []
    order = max(metas.values(), key=lambda d: len(d["segments"]))["segments"]
    out, prev = [], 0
    for seg in order:
        d = metas.get(seg)
        if d is None:          # replayed from a resumed checkpoint; no file of its own
            continue
        out.append((prev, d["frames"], seg))
        prev = d["frames"]
    return out

Proof from a log: G:\AI World Record\harness\logs\secret_5c.out reads "bomb: 115 spots tried (26 unreachable)... burn: 115 spots tried... push: 115 spots tried" — identical counts, so push is not scenery-gated. The current code cannot even emit the string "no targets".

   I checked all six tables (0x18410 + n*0x80) against the seven screens whose method this project verified; none groups them by method. "Same byte as 0x34, therefore push" carries no information.

3) THE TILE DATA SAYS THERE IS NOTHING TO PUSH. From knowledge\rooms.json: 0x28 has 212 rock tiles, 0 trees, 0 gravestones (BC-BF), 0 Armos (E0-E3), 0 pushable-set tiles. 0x48: 276 rock, 0/0/0/0. 5) THE REAL GAP, WHICH THE CLAIM UNDERSTATES. The claim is right that those two table rows prove nothing, but wrong about which rows. File times: knowledge\rupee_caves.md 2026-09-14 13:38 < journal\23 (the rewrite) 2026-09-14 18:25 < zelda\secrets.py 2026-09-15 10:24. The "no targets" wording is the old scenery-driven tool. So push was never tried — but the BOMB rows ("84 spots", "60 spots") are equally stale, because they predate the opening() baseline fix documented at secrets.py:32-40: the old detector "reported 'nothing opened' after 220 bombs at Spectacle Rock, a rock this run had already blown open. Every bomb secret on the map was invisible until this check." The claim treats the bomb sweeps as sound. They are not. Both methods need re-running, with the candle added.

rejected.title: The planner's price of time can never exceed the price of one hit, so waiting is always the cheapest move
rejected.why:
CLAIM REFUTED — arithmetic mostly right, mechanism and diagnosis wrong.

1. HEADLINE IS INVERTED. "Waiting is always the cheapest move" is false by the code's own numbers. A `wait` pays BOTH the time term and a dedicated extra: 0.5*u*6 + 25*u = 28*u (lookahead.py:263 and 269-270). A `hold` that moves Link pays only 0.5*u*8 = 4*u. Waiting is ~7x more expensive than walking at EVERY urgency level. It wins only if all four holds trigger the -120 wall penalty (line 273) and only while u < 5 (120 > 24*u). The planner already prices idling above the alternatives. Empirical proof: exactly 62 blank runs of length 6 — the wait macro's unique signature — exist in the entire 372,090-frame log (372 frames, 0.1%).

Verified-correct sub-claims: damage_weight=400.0 (line 90); `sc -= damage_weight*(before.hearts-after.hearts)*2` (line 97) with hearts a float half-step, so a half heart = 400 pts; URGENCY=7 (line 23); urgency 1.0->8.0 (line 198); wait is 6 frames (lines 27, 209); search.py:178 `r = x.hearts*600 - x.frames` prices half a heart at 300 frames; 800/300 = 2.67x. Minor slip: cost at u=1 is 25+3=28, not 31.

2. EVIDENCE NUMBERS REPLICATE, ATTRIBUTION DOES NOT. From logs/fullgame_run.inputs.txt I reproduce 2,583 runs/27,636 frames (6-12) and 318 runs/60,785 frames (45+) exactly; total idle 103,698/372,090 = 27.9%. But composition kills the causal story: 22,550 of the 27,636 frames are runs of EXACTLY 11 (2,050 of them) — the sword-swing animation tail `step((), 11)` at lookahead.py:47 and combat.py:72. That is the NES sword lockout, not discretionary waiting; no weight change removes a frame of it. In the 45+ bucket, ~14,258 frames are whirlwind rides (whirl_l6 4,946, whirl_back* 2,700, whirl_l3 954, hc_w37 2,102, ms_w22 2,080, rb_w0b 1,476) emitted by scripted `rec.step((), 30+rng)` / `rec.step((), 4)` loops in whirlwind_policy/whirl_to_policy (fullgame.py:510-514, 550-553) with no planner involved; 3,002 are g9_credits; ~3,000 are L*_done triforce scrolls; l4_32 930 + l4_40_key 864 are Fighter, not planner.

3. THE GLEEOK STAND IS AN EARLY-EXIT BUG, NOT A WEIGHTS PROBLEM (decisive). The 3,677-frame stand is real — one contiguous blank run from frame 60,987 to the segment end at 64,664 — and the trace shows Link frozen at x=120 y=113 dir=4 anim=0 mode=5 with kills=2 since frame 60,969 (boss already dead). But ALL FOUR successful attempts logged 6,019 / 6,018 / 6,012 / 6,020 frames against `gleeok_policy(nav, budget=6000)` (fullgame.py:133, 153). Every attempt burned the entire budget. `plan_fight`'s `while frames < max_frames` is released only by `finished()`, which defers wholly to `done(emu)` when done is supplied (lookahead.py:135-138). `gleeok_dead` (boss.py:215-224) returns True only if `$034D` is set, else falls through to `any(hp[i] >> 4 for i in range(1,8))` — which its OWN docstring says is "never true" after the boss dies because the game leaves stale values in the health slots. Once $034D fails to latch in L4 room 0x13 the predicate is stuck False forever. Proof it is room-specific and not the weights: the SAME gleeok_policy with the same weights exits early elsewhere — l6_mini 775 frames (budget 40,000) and l8_gleeok 1,443 frames (budget 10,000). Therefore reweighting returns ZERO frames at Gleeok: the loop cannot exit, so it fills the same 6,000 frames with holds and swings instead of waits — identical frame count, and Link pacing instead of standing, which is arguably worse on camera. The proposal's single largest named example is misdiagnosed.

4. THREE OF THE FOUR VALIDATION TARGETS BARELY TOUCH THE PLANNER. l4_32 (4,906 frames, 2,076 idle) is fullgame.py:1981 `make_clear_policy(nav, "Right")` -> segments.py:83-105 -> `Fighter.clear_room()`; combat.py imports only `UNKILLABLE, killable` from lookahead (combat.py:12) and never calls plan_fight/plan_reach, so editing lookahead.py changes it by exactly zero frames. l7_3a (3,135 frames) is bomb_policy (fullgame.py:2324) which reaches plan_fight only in the NavError fallback; its TOTAL idle is 122 frames. fd40 (10,043 frames, 1,772 idle) is farm_dungeon_policy calling plan_fight(max_frames=1500) inside a 6-cycle loop dominated by dungeon re-entry and navigation. Only gleeok is planner-dominated, and it is the bug case.

5. CORRECTED SAVING. The whole farm*/fd*/gleeok family is 65,146 frames with 15,648 idle, of which gleeok is 4,907 and 316 runs are len-11 swing tails. Net planner idle that a reweighting could plausibly recover is low single-thousands at most, not 24,000. Mechanically the proposed (a) is near-noise: raising time_weight 0.5->1.3 moves a hold's cost from 4 to 10.4 points against shaping terms of -0.6*dist and -want*d_item that reach several hundred (lines 232-259) and miss penalties of 150-400 (lines 241-247). Proposal (c) is actively harmful: decaying damage_weight to a 120 floor fights `random_search.rank()`, which subtracts `(4 - hearts) * 4000` below four hearts (search.py:179-180). A planner that trades hits produces attempts rank() discards, so searches lose the full-health early stop (`limit = patience` vs `patience*2`, search.py:198) and take roughly twice as long for worse hearts. The run already leaves L4 at 3.5/5. Expected net effect of the proposal as written: roughly 0-1,500 frames, plausibly negative. Separately, ~3,700 frames ARE genuinely available at Gleeok — from the correctly diagnosed done-predicate fix, not from the weights.

6. REPLAY/DETERMINISM: no break, but real cost. The verified artifact is a fixed input list; replay.verify compares sha1 of RAM 0..0x800 (replay.py:31-33, 36-45) and is unaffected by planner weights. However every checkpoint stores its input prefix (runner.py:67-74, 76-86), so re-searching gleeok invalidates all ~500 downstream segments; that segment alone cost 8,611s wall. And runner.py:125-126 raises "main diverged from scout" on any marginal attempt, so looser damage weights raise the hard-failure rate mid-run.

rejected.title: Patience is a constant while segment cost spans 50x: 76% of the wall clock goes to segments that exhaust their tries for almost no frame gain
rejected.why:
REFUTED — the diagnosis is mostly sound, the prescription saves WALL time and LOSES frames.

1) WHAT THE CODE ACTUALLY SHOWS (mostly confirmed)
- zelda/search.py:133 `prefer_hearts: bool = True, patience: int = 8` — confirmed.
- zelda/search.py:198 `limit = patience if best is not None and best.hearts >= s.containers else patience * 2` — confirmed.
- The call site is zelda/runner.py:114-116 (NOT harness/runner.py, which does not exist): `best = random_search(scout, start, factory(self.snav), success, tries=tries, max_frames=max_frames, label=name, log=self.log, prefer_hearts=True, setup=reset_beliefs)` — patience is never passed, so every segment gets 8/16. Confirmed.
- Wall concentration CONFIRMED: reconstructing the surviving chain from logs/fullgame.txt, 269 segments never early-stopped and consumed 48,376 of 63,258 attributable wall seconds = 76.5% (claim said 76%).
- Size of the big-segment bucket CONFIRMED: from the checkpoint chain, 70 segments >=1000 frames = 157,575 frames = 42% of 372,090 (claim: 71 / 158,590 / 44%).
- Early-stop stats CONFIRMED: 265 early-stopped, mean 18.8, median 18 (claim: 268 / 19.2 / 18). Median s/attempt >=1000 frames = 13.26 (claim 13.0).

2) WHERE THE EVIDENCE IS WRONG
- The tries histogram is fabricated. Calling fullgame.segments() gives 609 entries with tries = 40:340, 30:84, 50:62, 60:54, 20:32, 25:9, 12:8, 4:8, 10:7, 80:3, 8:1, 3:1 (budget 23,774). The claim's "40 (159), 20 (64), 50 (62), 60 (53), 30 (51), 80 (2)" sums to 391 and omits tries=3,4,8,10,12,25 entirely — i.e. it omits the cheapest-tries/most-expensive-frame segments: fd40, fd61, fd47, fd54 are tries=10; l8_gleeok is tries=12; g9_credits is tries=3.
- "328 ran ALL their tries" — actual 269.
- Per-attempt wall figures are off by 4-10x: farm53 is 41.8 s/attempt (1,671s / 40), not 417; farm63 is 45.5, not 182; white_sword is 41.6, not 105. Median under 1,000 frames is 0.39 s, not 0.6.
- The log cannot support the stated precision anyway: it is 180 appended sessions with 665 segment lines for a 610-segment run, and only 534 segments are recoverable with per-segment lines (339,329 of 372,090 frames).

3) THE SAVING IS THE WRONG SIGN
Simulating the PROPOSED rule against the real logged improvement traces (patience resets on each improvement, exactly as search.py:182-199 does), over the same 534 segments:
  CURRENT patience=8  -> 346,559 frames / 7,734 attempts
  PROPOSED f//120     -> 344,381 frames / 4,707 attempts
  CURRENT patience x2 -> 342,902 frames / 12,739 attempts
  PROPOSED f//120 x2  -> 341,340 frames / 8,236 attempts
  ACTUAL run          -> 339,329 frames
Against the actual run the proposal is +2,011 to +5,052 frames WORSE: 275 segments degrade (+8,613 frames total; worst: l5_66_key +1,074, g9_03 +286, digdogger +264, dodongo +263), only 22 improve. This is structural, not bad luck — fewer attempts can only equal or worsen the best found. Patience scaling is a wall-clock optimization with a negative frame expectation; it buys a genuine ~35-39% cut in attempts.

4) THE REINVESTMENT CANNOT COVER IT
All 8,000 claimed frames rest on "re-search the 71 big segments with 3x tries". Its own evidence caps that: 40 extra attempts across ~596 segments buy 3,971 frames (my re-derivation: k=20 343,577 -> k=60 339,907 = 3,670). Restricted to the big segments, attempts after 20 bought only 1,984 frames total. And 34 of 69 big segments ALREADY exhaust all their tries, so 3x tries is the only lever and it is on the flat part of the curve. The proof case is gleeok: tries=80, 7,978s (2.2h) of wall, and the kept attempt is 1 frame WORSE than attempt 1 (6019 -> 6020) because rank() at search.py:178 trades ~600 frames per half heart. farm43 and farm53 ran all 40 attempts for a gain of exactly 0 frames.

5) THE WALL BUDGET IS BACKWARDS
Big segments already consume 41,524s (11.5h) of the 17.6h attributable; cheap ones only 21,734s (6.0h). Tripling tries on the big set adds ~+23.1h. Deleting ALL cheap-segment search saves at most 6.0h. The package is net roughly +17h of wall, not "5-7 hours freed".

6) ARCHITECTURAL BLOCKER — segments cannot be re-searched in isolation
grep "splice" hits only a docstring (search.py:5); no splice tooling exists. runner.py:99-100 saves the search start state from MAIN's live state, and :122-126 plays the winner into MAIN then asserts `if not success(main, s): raise RuntimeError(f"segment {name}: main diverged from scout")`. Every downstream segment's input list was recorded from one specific predecessor state, so re-searching a segment invalidates everything after it. The earliest big segment is index 61 of 610 (l1_45_key), so "re-search only the 71 big segments" is in fact a re-run of ~90% of the game.

7) IT TARGETS THE WRONG THING FOR THE OWNER'S GOAL
Of the 157,575 frames in big segments, 59,124 (12 segments: farm33/43/53/63/68/73/78/83, fd40/47/54/61) are rupee/bomb grinding — which is the owner's complaint #2 (stop buying bombs, buy capacity upgrades, delete the farming), a route/economy change worth far more than search tuning. Another 9,561 is whirlwind rides (fixed duration), 3,002 is the end credits (g9_credits, tries=3). No number of extra attempts compresses any of those.

rejected.title: The bomb-buying trip the owner complained about cost 17,429 frames; the run already has a 98-frame alternative it wrote itself
rejected.why:
MIXED, and refuted on the part that matters. The cost figure is exactly right; the proposed replacement mechanism does not work.

1) THE COST IS REAL AND EXACT. G:\AI World Record\harness\fullgame.py lines 2637-2688 (the claim says 2637-2679; the block actually ends at rb_16b on 2688) are 36 segments. Summing their lines in G:\AI World Record\harness\logs\fullgame.txt gives 17,429 frames, and the frame counter agrees independently: s9_25 ends at "total 330143 frames", rb_16b at "total 347572" -> 17,429. 4.83 minutes. The behaviour is as described: leave L9 (rb_26..rb_out), whirlwind to L4's island door (rb_w45), raft (rb_sail/rb_land/rb_shore), walk the lake (rb_65/64/54/44), buy 4 bombs for 20 rupees (rb_buy1, rup 77->57), exit, buy 4 more (rb_buy2, 57->37), exit, whirlwind back (rb_w0b, 1671 frames), walk the mountain road (rb_r1b..rb_r05), re-enter (rb_enter) and RE-FIGHT the whole entrance wing (rb_66/56/55/55_st/pass2/15b/16b = 4,109 frames), because fullgame.py:2617 notes "The entrance wing refills when Link re-enters the dungeon". The stated cause matches journal/28-zero-bombs.md and the comment at fullgame.py:2627-2636.

2) THE 98-FRAME ALTERNATIVE DOES NOT TRANSPLANT. This is the refutation. bomb_drop_policy (fullgame.py:1662) has two hard guards before it does anything:
   fullgame.py:1686  if (cyc0 + 1) % 10 not in (1, 6, 8): return f"kill cycle {cyc0}: the next kill is not a bomb column"
   fullgame.py:1688  if not reds(emu): return "no Red Wizzrobe here"
and reds() is defined at fullgame.py:1677 as `[x for x in read_enemies(e) if x[1] == RED_WIZZROBE]`, RED_WIZZROBE = 0x24 (fullgame.py:1649). It only ever earns a bomb from a Red Wizzrobe.
   The entrance wing has none. Row 2 is the only row with bombs, and per knowledge/level9_route.md it is types 09 0A 03 01 12 06 0B 24 30 = Blue Octoroks, Blue Moblin, Blue Lynel, Vire, Red Goriya, Red Darknut, Red Wizzrobe, Gibdo (names from zelda/overworld.py:28-42). The wing's contents, from knowledge/level9_route.md plus the ROM monster bytes via zelda/romdata.room_info(9, r):
     0x76 monsters=0x00 (none) | 0x66 old man | 0x56 =0xb3 | 0x55 Lanmolas | 0x14 five Like Likes (0x17) | 0x15 =0x23 Blue Wizzrobe | 0x16 Patra | 0x26 eight Gels (0x15) | 0x25 Bubbles/Zols/Like Likes
   Like Like 0x17, Gel 0x14/0x15 are on the explicit "No drops at all" list; Blue Wizzrobe 0x23 is drop ROW 0 (22 18 22 18 23 18 22 22 18 18) which contains no bombs at all; Zol 0x13 is row 3, also no bombs. The wizzrobe-bearing ROM monster bytes in L9 are 0x7b (rooms 05,20,35,40,54,57), 0xf7 (04,30) and 0xf1 (07,10,47,65,73) - NONE of which is an entrance-wing room. So applying bomb_drop_policy in the wing returns "no Red Wizzrobe here" on every attempt. Proposal leg (1) is dead as written.

3) THE 98 FRAMES IS ALSO A BEST-OF-SEARCH NUMBER, NOT A REPEATABLE COST. logs/probe_bombdrop.out: attempts 2, 6 and 7 succeeded out of 15 (151, 150, 98 frames) and knowledge/level9_route.md records "3 of 15 probe attempts, 3 of 23 in the run". It works at 0x04 only because the kill cycle happens to be 0 there so the next kill is column 1. Anywhere else the column guard must also be satisfied.

4) THE OTHER IN-PLACE SOURCE IS ALSO GONE. It did not come back on re-entry: r9_16 (fullgame.py:2625) uses make_lafight_policy, whose plan_fight applies the bomb-seeking shaping at zelda/lookahead.py:250-259 (want += 1.5 + 2.5 when bombs < 4) and then calls Fighter.collect_drop, whose DROPS table (zelda/combat.py:590) includes 0x00 "bombs". Link cleared 0x16 with that pull active and still had zero bombs (fullgame.py:2627). Monsters refill on re-entry; a taken room item does not.

5) WHAT IS GENUINELY SALVAGEABLE. The trip IS wasteful and the owner's complaint is justified, but the fix is proposal leg (2)/(3), not leg (1): carry bombs in rather than earn them there. Ledger: m9_16_bombs banked 4; between it and r9_enter the run spends 18,924 frames over 31 segments (the Magical Sword / heart-container detour) including hc_2c_heart (bombs a rock) and r9_enter itself (bomb_entry_policy, fullgame.py:2613, one bomb to open Spectacle Rock), plus planner throws - arriving at zero. Perfect conservation still only yields ~2, and the route needs 4 walls minimum after 0x16 (0x06->0x05, 0x20->0x10, 0x31->0x30, 0x04->0x03) plus planner throws. So a purchase is still required; it just should be folded into the overworld detour the run is ALREADY making, instead of a dedicated round trip.

6) SIZING. Deletable: rb_* 17,429 + s9_26/s9_25 614 (the failed grab at the walled-off 0x25 pile, which only exists because Link had no bombs) = 18,043. Replacement cost: a shop detour inside the existing hc_*/ms_* overworld loop, realistically ~1,500-4,000 frames (for reference the rb trip's pure shopping core, rb_w45 through rb_leave2, is 3,757). Net ~14,000-16,500. I put the defensible figure at ~14,000 rather than the claimed 16,000, because the claim assumed a zero-cost in-place replacement that does not exist.

7) LEG (3) IS CONFUSED. The 100-rupee bomb CAPACITY upgrade raises MaxBombs; it creates no bombs, so it does not fix "arrived at zero". ram.MAX_BOMBS = 0x67C (zelda/ram.py:50) is defined but read nowhere in the codebase. Per journal/28-zero-bombs.md the upgrades are in Levels 5 and 7, both long past by Level 9, and the run's only other shops (buy_arrows fullgame.py:2176, buy_food 2304) are earlier still - so there is no "shopping trip the run is already making" at this point in the route. Worth doing for the owner's stated rule, but it is not part of this saving.

8) RULES / DETERMINISM. Nothing here breaks the owner's rules. Checkpoints are search bookmarks only: zelda/emulator.py load()/mload() set `input_log_valid = False`, emu.inputs is "one entry per emulated frame since power-on", and zelda/replay.py replays that flat list from power-on and compares a SHA1 of all 2KB of RAM. bomb_drop_policy is legitimate play - it reads the public drop table and fights, with the search retrying from a bookmark, exactly the established method. No memory writes, no savestates in the trajectory, no glitch abuse. BUT the change is not local: editing the segment list at 2637 invalidates every recorded input after it - 37 segments and 24,518 frames from s9_06 to g9_credits must be re-searched, and the whole run re-verified by replay from power-on.

BONUS FINDING (not part of this claim): the 0x43 dead end the journal admits was a wrong deduction is still in the list - s9_43 (fullgame.py:2701), s9_43_text, s9_b53, s9_b63 = 4,773 frames and one wasted bomb, for an old man saying "PATRA HAS THE MAP". Deleting it saves frames AND one of the bombs this whole dispute is about.

rejected.title: Learned knowledge (tiles.json, blocks.json) mutates mid-run, is never reset between attempts, and is a write race under parallel scouts
rejected.why:
MIXED CODE FACTS, REFUTED DIAGNOSIS, ZERO FRAMES.

(1) What's TRUE. The cited lines are accurate. `TileKB.learn()` ends with `self.save()` (overworld.py:101) and `save()` does `self.path.write_text(...)` (77-80), so every learned tile rewrites knowledge/tiles.json immediately. `remember_block()` rewrites blocks.json at overworld.py:604. runner.py:109-117 snapshots and restores only `self.snav.blocked`, and the comment at 104-107 is verbatim as quoted. The KB is indeed never reset between attempts. One correction to the claim's model: main and scout do NOT share one KB today — Navigator.__init__ (overworld.py:333) does `kb or TileKB()`, and runner.py:45-46 builds two Navigators, so there are two independent in-memory KBs loaded at open(); they interact only through the file.

(2) "Write race under parallel scouts" — REFUTED. There are no parallel scouts. `grep -rn "multiprocessing|threading|Thread\(|concurrent.futures|Pool\(|asyncio|fork\("` over the whole harness returns nothing. runner.py drives exactly one main and one scout sequentially. run_until.sh enforces one run at a time with an atomic `mkdir /tmp/zelda_run.lock` plus a PID-liveness check, and PLAN.md ("Operating the run, learned the hard way, twice") documents concurrent runs as the thing to never do. The only genuine concurrent-writer hazard is an ad-hoc probe run alongside a run — all ~100 probe scripts do `Navigator(emu)` → their own TileKB → whole-file overwrite, last-writer-wins — which is an operational hazard, not an in-run race, and costs no frames.

(3) Frames — REFUTED on two independent grounds.
  (a) Structural: a failed attempt contributes ZERO frames. runner.segment only appends the winner (`for b in best.inputs: main.step(b, 1)`, runner.py:122-123). A total segment failure raises RuntimeError → run_until.sh restarts → `resume` reloads the checkpoint → nothing added. So KB pollution can only cost wall-clock search time, never game frames, unless it lengthens the *winning* attempt.
  (b) Empirical: `learn()` is the ONLY caller of `save()` (overworld.py:101; no other KB_PATH writer exists repo-wide), so tiles.json's mtime IS the timestamp of the last tile ever learned: 2026-09-15 11:32. The checkpoints written at 11:32 are fullgame_ms_21/ms_31/ms_32/ms_w22 (the Magical Sword). Every segment from 11:44 (r9_w0b) through 18:56 (g9_credits) — all of r9_*, s9_*, rb_*, g9_*, roughly 250 of the 609 entries — ran with the tile KB completely static. It cannot have cost frames there.

(4) The offered evidence is misattributed. The room-55 "no path to the Down edge" failures (fullgame.txt:3454 and 3460, 24x/13x/3x/2x) are the raft-timing bug, and the codebase says so itself. settle_policy's docstring, fullgame.py:1526-1531: "dock_policy's segments succeed the moment the screen changes, but the raft keeps sailing Link down the channel to the pier after that. The next segment then planned from open water - 'no path to the Down edge from (128,90)' - or pressed Up and sailed straight back to the island." That is the exact log string. The failing positions (128,81)→(128,90)→(128,102)→(128,117)→(128,127) trace the raft sailing down the lake; journal/29 covers the (128,127) case as the Octorok knocking Link back onto the dock. tiles.json's ow `evidence` dict contains no room-55 entry at all, so no tile was ever learned on that screen. Both failures were fixed by ADDING segments (rb_land at fullgame.py:2653, rb_shore at 2659), not by touching the KB; the winners came in at 65 and 151 frames. The 37-of-40 pier failure the runner comment describes was the `blocked` bug, already fixed — and `blocked` in fact never accumulates across segments at all, since blocked0 is re-snapshotted each segment and restored at line 117.

(5) Honest steelman. The mechanism is not impossible: the NavError text is "...even through unknown tiles", i.e. optimistic=True, where `is_walkable` trusts unknown ids but still refuses anything in `solid` — so only an explicit solid entry can block an optimistic plan. And there IS a real latent bug nearby: overworld.py:537 learns walkable only `if t not in self.kb.walkable and t not in self.kb.solid`, so a falsely-learned SOLID tile can never be corrected by standing on it, and it is persisted forever. That deserves a fix — but no instance is demonstrable in this run, and the proposed change does not address it.

(6) Replay/stability. The change cannot break the existing MATCH: replay.verify (replay.py:36-44) replays the saved input file from power-on and hashes RAM; the KB is not involved, and the verified log is already on disk. But the proposal carries a real stability REGRESSION: making learning in-memory and flushing "once at finish()" loses everything on every crash, and fullgame.txt contains 180 "resumed checkpoint" lines (run_until.sh exists precisely because "the emulator process dies silently every so often"); save_checkpoint (runner.py:67-74) does not persist the KB either. Worse, resetting kb.ctx per attempt is counterproductive in a way the `blocked` reset is not: `blocked` holds (pos, dir) pairs that are often transient false positives from a knockback, whereas tile solidity is a global property of a pattern id — learning it once on attempt 1 is what saves attempts 2-40 from repeating the same failed step. Resetting it makes the search re-bump the same wall up to 40 times per segment.
